Jersey Water is evaluating a new treatment plant to reduce PFAS levels in drinking water, following recommendations from a scientific panel, despite the high potential cost to islanders.

The Poison:
The high cost of the solution could lead to the most expensive water bills in the world, creating a secondary crisis of affordability for residents.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
There is no plane error here. The report correctly identifies the WHAT (PFAS levels), the WHO (Jersey Water/Government), and the HOW (treatment plants/costs).

The Unavoidable Truth: PFAS contamination requires expensive infrastructure to mitigate.

The Unavoidable Lie: There is a cheap, easy way to remove these chemicals from the water supply.
